course_name_original: Globalization. New Challenges in the Contemporary World
course_name_en: Globalization. New Challenges in the Contemporary World

learning_outcomes.text: Knows at a basic level the non-technical conditions of changes occurring in the contemporary world in philosophical, cultural, economic, legal, historical, religious, political and social dimensions. Understands the functioning of contemporary society and its philosophical, cultural, economic, legal, historical, religious, political and social conditions.
Understands the principles of market mechanisms in the contemporary world.

Is able to work independently on a research problem based on independently selected scientific sources; is able to prepare an oral statement or written text regarding non-technical conditions of changes occurring in society from a philosophical, cultural, economic, legal, historical, religious, political and social perspective.
Is able to integrate knowledge from various bibliographic sources and databases in Polish and English (or another language recognized as a language of international scientific communication).

Is able to write a scientific text in Polish and a foreign language (recognized as a language of international scientific communication), which is a well-documented bibliographic study of a given problem, in accordance with the requirements of substantive and linguistic correctness. Is able to characterize changes in contemporary society from a philosophical, cultural, legal, economic and social perspective based on independently selected scientific sources.
Is aware of the scope of their current knowledge and understands the need for continuous self-education and self-development.

Understands the consequences of technical and engineering activity in the natural and social environment. Is aware of responsibility for decisions made in the field of engineering activities. Demonstrates an pro-ecological attitude.

syllabus_topics: What does it mean to live in a global field? Introduction of basic concepts. The concept of capitalism as a world system by I. Wallerstein will be discussed as a prolegomena to globalization. R. Roberston's theory of globalization and glocalization will be presented. The main concepts related to these theories will be explained.

Global network society – a look at social relations. Global society as a network society in M. Castells' view: the problem of global flows and exclusion. Social shifts: changes in the social role of states and cities.

World risk society and its consequences. Discussion of U. Beck's concept of risk society, its global reach. The dilemma of risk as knowledge and ignorance as sources of uncertainty and anti-scientific movements.
Capital flows, marketization of culture – an economic perspective. Economic globalization, institutionalization of global capitalism and its contestation (anti-globalism and alter-globalism).

Globalization of threats - economic aspect. Problems of international and transnational security in the era of globalization. Black market, illegal transnational economic activities. The problem of state borders and their permeability.

Migrations in times of globalization – basic information about world demography. Presentation of demographic processes in the contemporary world. First and second demographic transition. Regional variations and general trends as pro-migration factors. Global migrations as a consequence of capitalism. Migration networks. Cultural connections and global myths as a cultural factor of migration.

Does everyone have to be a tourist? Sociology of mobility. Ambiguity of the category of tourist. Tourists and vagabonds as a structure of the postmodern world (Z. Bauman). Transnational cultures (U. Hannerz).

Cultural landscapes of the global world: media, political and ethnic. Political globalization: regulations and deregulability. The power of globalization (J. Staniszkis). Do media create a global village? Cultural mosaics as a result of global processes. Political threats.

Sociology of mobility. Tourism as a globalized self-image. How spatial practices organize today's life (J. Urry). Forms of transnational spaces: global cities, tourist cities. Consequences of migration for abandoned areas.
Why don't we think seriously about the environment? The problem of climate change; social reactions to environmental threats. Social reactions to COVID-19.
Religion in times of globalization. Global religions. Transformations of religion in global processes – fundamentalism and liberalization.
assessment_rules: Students participate in classes, learning subsequent teaching content according to the course syllabus. Students should ask questions and clarify doubts on an ongoing basis. Audiovisual recording of the lecture requires the consent of the instructor.
